description.en: Northern arm of the A3, running from Târgu Mureș through Cluj-Napoca and Zalău to the Hungarian border at Borș, where it meets the M4. Originally contracted to Bechtel in 2003 as a single design-build-finance deal; that contract was terminated in 2013 after the company delivered only 52 of the contracted kilometres, and the remaining lots were re-tendered with EU financing. Sections opened in stages from 2009; the mountainous Nușfalău–Zimbor stretch through the Meseș tunnel is the last major gap.
description.ro: Ramura nordică a A3, de la Târgu Mureș prin Cluj-Napoca și Zalău până la granița cu Ungaria la Borș, unde se leagă de autostrada M4. Contractată inițial cu Bechtel în 2003 într-un singur contract de proiectare-construcție-finanțare; acel contract a fost reziliat în 2013, după ce compania livrase doar 52 din kilometrii contractați, iar loturile rămase au fost relicitate cu finanțare europeană. Tronsoanele s-au deschis etapizat din 2009; porțiunea montană Nușfalău–Zimbor, cu tunelul Meseș, este ultimul gol major.

contract.noticeReference: First Romanian motorway completed in 2020: opened 4 September 2020, connecting directly to the Hungarian motorway network

detail.en: EU funds, after the Bechtel contract was terminated in 2013
detail.ro: Fonduri europene, după rezilierea contractului cu Bechtel în 2013

contract.noticeReference: Biharia–Chiribiș (28.55 km) and Chiribiș–Suplacu de Barcău (26.35 km) re-tendered after the Bechtel termination; OpenStreetMap tags opening_date=2026 on subsection 3A lot 2
Section of the Transylvania motorway re-tendered with EU financing after the 2013 Bechtel termination

Last major gap of the Transylvania motorway, including the Meseș tunnel — Romania's longest road tunnel when complete. OpenStreetMap tags opening_date=2032 on Tunel Meseș and subsections 3B3/3B4/3B lot 3; the 31 km Nușfalău–Poarta Sălajului lot was still in tender at the technical-project stage

Nădășelu–Mihăiești (16.85 km) contracted May 2016 for €100M with an 18-month term; design was delayed because the feasibility study proved inadequate. OpenStreetMap tags opening_date=2026 on subsection 3B1 (Mihăiești–Zimbor) and the Nădășelu route deviation

First 42 km of the Transylvania motorway, opened 1 December 2009; built under the 2003 Bechtel design-build-finance contract, whose ground-breaking was held at Chinteni (Cluj) on 16 June 2004. Bechtel delivered 52 of the contracted kilometres before termination in 2013
Final 10–12 km delivered by Bechtel on the Câmpia Turzii–Gilău section, inaugurated 13 November 2010
Iernut–Ungheni was the first segment of this section opened, on 12 December 2018, after the Geiger and Strabag lots were finished; the Cluj-Napoca West (Gilău)–Nădășelu extension followed in 2018
